description: Given a binary tree (not necessarily perfect), populate each next pointer to point to its next right node. If there is no next right node, the next pointer should be set to NULL.
intuition: Unlike the perfect binary tree version, children may be missing. Use a dummy node to build a linked list of the next level while traversing the current level via its next pointers. The dummy's next becomes the head of the next level's chain.
approach: Use a dummy node to build the next level while traversing the current level using next pointers. The dummy node acts as the head of the linked list for the next level.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: root = [1,2,3,4,5,null,7]

Level 0: node = node(1)
  dummy -> null, curr = dummy
  node(1): left=node(2), right=node(3)
    curr.next = node(2), curr = node(2)
    curr.next = node(3), curr = node(3)
    node = node(1).next = null -> inner while ends
  node = dummy.next = node(2)

Level 1: node = node(2)
  dummy -> null, curr = dummy
  node(2): left=node(4), right=node(5)
    curr.next = node(4), curr = node(4)
    curr.next = node(5), curr = node(5)
    node = node(2).next = node(3)
  node(3): left=null, right=node(7)
    curr.next = node(7), curr = node(7)
    node = node(3).next = null
  inner while ends
  node = dummy.next = node(4)
  node(4).next -> node(5), node(5).next -> node(7) are set

Level 2: node(4), all leaves, no children to link
  node = dummy.next = null -> outer while ends

Result: [1,#,2,3,#,4,5,7,#]
explanation:
1. Process one level at a time using next pointers.
2. Use a dummy node as the head of the next level linked list.
3. For each node at the current level, connect its children to the next level list.
4. After processing the current level, move to dummy.next (start of next level).
5. Works for any binary tree, not just perfect trees.
hints: Unlike problem 116, the tree may not be perfect, so some children may be missing.
Use a dummy node to simplify building the next level list.
Traverse the current level using next pointers set in the previous iteration.
